title: Two-sided retained grafts face shared shutdown; catalytic persistence cannot create missing fibre contact
status_authority: Actual version-bound scoped internal review governs acceptance. Source reports, mathematical verification and physical acquisition remain separate.
reported_status: accepted_internally_verified for the declared independent-arm, Poisson/shared-clock and contact-race mathematical scopes. Enzymatic wet welding and regenerative repair remain unacquired proposals; all mechanical and molecular parameters are hypothetical.
scientific_scope_status: Independent linker arms that make mechanically retained old/new grafts with total probability u and old-side fraction theta give Pcross=1-(1-u*theta)^v-(1-u*(1-theta))^v+(1-u)^v. For symmetric four-arm old/new access, shared access time T~Exp(d), arm hazard k and retention eta>0, Poisson mean N candidate linkers have zero-weld probability E[exp(-N*P4(1-exp(-k*T)))], with N^-1/2 rather than naive exponential abundance scaling. A guaranteed catalytic period T0>0 gives a positive probability floor and exponential upper bound, but independent contact-before-shutdown has ceiling g/(g+d). Chemical grafts, wet load transfer and repeated living regeneration remain separate evidence claims.
